purpose: Virginia large-load ledger linking reported data-center load-drop events to regulatory cost-allocation and reliability responses, while preserving the open household-incidence and geopolitical-leverage stages.

events.geography: United States; Virginia electric system and Dominion large-load service context
events.date_precision: July 2024 utility-reported event; exact outage date, duration, facility roster, and feeder geography are not retained
events.denominator: Aggregate utility-reported large-load event; 1,551 MW dropped after a 230 kV outage, not a household or facility-level denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the retained Virginia large-load governance layer and official regulatory source notes
events.missingness: No site-level identity, outage duration, household service effect, worker effect, cost, bill, backup-generation cost, or independent reconstruction is retained
events.exposure: Dominion reported 1,551 MW of data-center load dropped after a 230 kV outage and transferred to backup generation
events.alternatives_before_action: Backup generation and system operating alternatives are reported in aggregate; facility-level response choice and customer alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The event demonstrates operational load flexibility or stress; local reliability, fuel cost, emissions, and household burden are not measured
events.choice_or_response: Large-load behavior entered system operations; specific facility dispatch, curtailment, or service choice is not identified
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Utility and large-load customers controlled operational response within grid constraints; regulator authority and customer obligations were not yet fully represented in this event
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The event contributed to the policy context for large-load reliability and cost-allocation governance; no event-specific remedy is observed
events.immediate_outcome: A utility-reported large-load operational event is visible
events.protected_outcome: System operation may have protected broader reliability; household service protection is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Facility operations, backup-generation resources, or local reliability may have carried costs; no incidence is observed
events.cost_risk_transfer: Operational stress could shift cost or reliability risk among large-load firms, utilities, and ratepayers, but the direction is not identified
events.later_outcome: Later regulatory response is documented at policy level; facility, household, worker, trust, action, and geopolitical outcomes remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: No resident or facility-level fairness, attribution, trust, or legitimacy judgment is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: No event-specific complaint, public input, organizing, or political response is linked
events.counterexample: A large-load drop can protect system reliability while disrupting a facility; the event alone does not identify net welfare or permanent curtailment
events.source_and_uncertainty: Retained Virginia governance layer and utility/regulatory source notes; aggregate utility reporting does not identify facilities, duration, or household effects

events.geography: United States; Virginia State Corporation Commission large-load governance
events.date_precision: November 2025 SCC order; GS-5 provisions effective January 2027
events.denominator: Large-load customers demanding at least 25 MW; initial filing later identified 139 accounts, including 131 data-center accounts and 8 non-data-center accounts
events.method: Structured extraction from the retained SCC order/release and Dominion High Load Customer Proposal source notes
events.missingness: No current roster, facility-level consumption, customer contract, actual payment, enforcement, household bill, local service cost, or affected-resident response is retained
events.exposure: Large-load growth and operational stress prompted a state rate class and minimum-demand governance response
events.alternatives_before_action: Customers could face different siting, interconnection, load, contract, or backup options; facility-level alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: GS-5 establishes minimum-demand provisions including 85% of contracted transmission/distribution demand and 60% of generation demand; realized payment and burden are not observed
events.choice_or_response: The state adopted a rate class and obligations intended to reduce nonperformance and cost-shifting risk; customer compliance and response remain unobserved
events.person_or_actor_with_control: SCC controls tariff and regulatory terms; utilities implement filings and large-load customers face the obligations; residents have no linked decision record
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: GS-5, minimum-demand provisions, and related collateral/term/interconnection governance are adopted or scheduled for implementation
events.immediate_outcome: Infrastructure dependence becomes an explicit regulatory allocation and reliability object
events.protected_outcome: The rules may protect system cost recovery or reliability; avoided residential cost and actual service protection are not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Large-load customers may face minimum-demand or contract obligations; customer, worker, resident, and local-service trade-offs are not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The policy attempts to move some infrastructure risk toward customers creating large demand, but actual cost allocation is unobserved
events.later_outcome: Implementation is scheduled for 2027; actual payments, defaults, enforcement, household bills, trust, political action, and geopolitical leverage remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The regulatory record makes cost-shifting arguments visible but contains no linked resident legitimacy or fairness outcome
events.public_or_collective_response: SCC proceedings and filings create a public input/governance route; participation and later political response are not linked
events.counterexample: A minimum-demand rule can improve cost recovery while increasing fixed obligations or reducing flexibility for some large-load customers
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official SCC order/release and Dominion filing summaries; policy design and initial account snapshot are not realized payment or household-incidence data

events.geography: United States; Virginia SCC Rider T1 proceeding and typical residential reference customer
events.date_precision: 2026 Rider T1 proceeding; exact filing/decision date and implementation status are source-specific
events.denominator: Modeled typical residential customer using 1,000 kWh/month; not observed households or bills
events.method: Structured extraction from retained SCC Rider T1 source notes and Virginia large-load governance layer
events.missingness: No residential account, bill, payment, actual allocation, facility causal share, hardship, trust, action, or exit is retained
events.exposure: The SCC describes a modeled typical-residential Rider T1 increase of $2.90/month before an amended allocation method and $0.94/month after it, a 67.5% reduction in the modeled increase
events.alternatives_before_action: Residential customers' supplier, conservation, payment, assistance, and non-use alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The modeled allocation comparison indicates a projected ratepayer-cost difference; it is not an observed bill or data-center-only attribution
events.choice_or_response: The regulator evaluates or models an amended allocation method; household response and facility payment behavior are not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: SCC controls methodology and approval; utilities and large-load customers influence filings; residential customers are represented only by a modeled reference case
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Amended Rider T1 allocation methodology is modeled as reducing the typical residential increase
events.immediate_outcome: A projected household-incidence comparison is visible in the regulatory record
events.protected_outcome: The amended method may reduce projected residential allocation relative to an alternative method; actual savings are not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Potential ratepayer cost remains modeled; actual affordability, payment, disconnection, and service sacrifice are unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The proceeding makes distributional cost allocation legible while leaving actual incidence and causal responsibility unresolved
events.later_outcome: No observed bill, payment, hardship, trust, political action, switching, or exit outcome is linked
events.meaning_and_attribution: Regulatory attribution is visible; resident fairness, legitimacy, and trust response are unobserved
events.public_or_collective_response: The docket supplies a public governance route; household participation and political action are not linked
events.counterexample: The $0.94 modeled illustration is not the same object as a reported $9.69 charge or an observed household bill; methods and rate components differ
events.source_and_uncertainty: Retained SCC Rider T1 source note and governance layer; values are modeled/filed illustrations and cannot be converted into household incidence or causal data-center attribution

events.method: Structured extraction from retained Dominion filing source note and Virginia governance layer

events.exposure: A filing identifies an initial large-load customer class and its data-center composition
events.alternatives_before_action: Alternative interconnection, siting, load, or supplier choices are not observed for the accounts
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The filing makes the scope of the proposed large-load governance class visible; actual cost and service outcomes are not observed
events.choice_or_response: Dominion filed a proposed customer framework; customer acceptance, negotiation, payment, and compliance are not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Utility filing and SCC review shape terms; individual customers and residents have no linked response record
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The filing supplies an implementation/accountability surface for GS-5 terms
events.immediate_outcome: The potential governed account population is enumerated for one filing snapshot
events.protected_outcome: A defined account class could support future cost/reliability accountability; no realized protection is established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Customer flexibility, facility investment, utility risk, and resident cost effects remain unknown

events.later_outcome: Current roster, consumption, payment, enforcement, household, trust, action, switching, and geopolitical outcomes remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: No customer or resident fairness, attribution, trust, or legitimacy endpoint is observed

events.geography: United States; Virginia State Corporation Commission and Dominion Energy Virginia
events.date_precision: SCC final-order date; supplemental direct-connect docket opened August 25, 2026
events.denominator: One final Rider T1 proceeding, PUR-2026-00056, and one supplemental line-extension proceeding, PUR-2026-00131; revenue and projected residential values are proceeding-level figures
events.method: Structured extraction from the Virginia SCC public facts page describing the final order and supplemental docket
events.missingness: No account-level bills, payments, actual direct-connect cost, customer compliance, construction, residential hardship, service change, trust, or political response is retained
events.exposure: Rapidly expanding large-load customers created a regulatory cost-allocation and direct-connect governance problem for transmission-related costs
events.alternatives_before_action: The Commission could retain the prior allocation method, assign costs prospectively to large-load customers, or use other tariff and line-extension terms; counterfactual system and household outcomes are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The SCC approved an amended allocation method and a framework requiring Dominion to modify its line-extension policy so qualifying direct-connect facilities are funded by the large-load customer that requires them
events.choice_or_response: The Commission approved the amended methodology in PUR-2026-00056 and established PUR-2026-00131 for Dominion's proposed line-extension amendments
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The SCC controls approval and methodology; Dominion must file amendments; large-load customers may bear direct-connect costs; residential customers remain an unlinked modeled class
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The final order creates a prospective direct-assignment framework and supplemental implementation docket, while retaining authority to adjust reforms if insufficient
events.immediate_outcome: A modeled typical residential Rider T1 increase was reported as falling from $2.90 to $0.94 per month under the approved amended method; the final order also created a concrete implementation route
events.protected_outcome: The approved framework is intended to protect existing customers from subsidizing direct-connect facilities needed only for new or expanding large loads; actual protection is not measured
events.sacrificed_outcome: Large-load customers may face direct-connect contributions, minimum-demand obligations, or reduced siting flexibility; actual payments and business responses are unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The decision attempts to transfer direct-connect infrastructure risk toward the large-load customer causing the need, while broader transmission allocation and actual residential incidence remain unresolved
events.later_outcome: As of the SCC public summary posted September 3, 2026, PUR-2026-00131 is still described as the docket that will receive Dominion's proposed amendments; a September 18 follow-up search found no later official indexed filing or Commission approval of those amendments. Customer payment, construction, enforcement, household bills, hardship, trust, and political response remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: The SCC publicly frames the reform as protecting existing customers and addressing cost allocation; no linked resident or customer legitimacy judgment is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: The proceeding provides a public regulatory route and supplemental docket; participant-level public input and later collective action are not linked
events.counterexample: Approval of a cost-allocation framework can coexist with no actual direct-connect construction, customer payment, or reduction in residential bills
events.source_and_uncertainty: Virginia SCC facts page posted September 3, 2026, describing the July 31, 2026 final order and August 25, 2026 supplemental docket; September 18 follow-up search found no later official indexed implementation filing. Approved policy and modeled effects are not observed incidence

boundary: This ledger formalizes a Virginia infrastructure-governance sequence from utility-reported large-load operational stress through state rate-class and projected allocation responses. It does not establish household bill incidence, net local benefit, resident legitimacy, practical exit, or geopolitical leverage.
storage_boundary: No utility customer account, facility telemetry, household bill, direct identifier, or restricted docket material is retained; only bounded public event/policy fields, denominators, modeled values, uncertainty, and open arrows are represented.
